audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing anywhere, and it was right: every reference to Wither was qualitative ("respect Wither", "trade around Wither's cooldown") with no number attached.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s on a 5-second slow at 700 range. That arithmetic is the whole lane: a spent Wither buys Teemo roughly ten seconds of free step-up, and there is no other tool in the Nasus kit that can touch a kiting Teemo. Without the numbers the player has no way to know how long the window lasts.
audit.corrected: Step up only in the ~10s gap between Wither expiring and coming back; hold Move Quick to break the slow rather than spending it for speed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the Sands was never described in either layer beyond the generic line "Nasus's ultimate changes the math too".
audit.why: Fury of the Sands halves Siphoning Strike's cooldown for its duration and grants Nasus bonus attack range on top of bonus Armor and Magic Resist. Both of those invalidate the kite spacing a Teemo player has spent the whole lane learning — his Q lands roughly twice as often and he can reach further while it is up.
audit.corrected: For the 15s his ult is up, kite wider than usual and expect Siphoning Strike about twice as often.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q was written as "Blinding Shot" in early, mid and whys[4].
audit.why: Riot's name for Teemo's Q is Blinding Dart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike is treated as a spell cast throughout; the fact that it is an auto-attack reset is never stated.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike resets Nasus's basic attack timer, so the visual tell is the attack wind-up rather than a cast animation. A player watching for a spell effect steps back too late.
audit.corrected: Read the attack wind-up, not a cast — Siphoning Strike rides on his basic attack.

audit.why: 50.64% over 628 games; content.late's EVEN verdict is consistent with it.

edits.before: At level 1 Nasus wins the first exchange more reliably than you expect — his passive lifesteal instantly heals a chunk of your E poison, and if he gets one Siphoning Strike Q on a cannon minion he is already even on the trade. Do not walk up to auto him repeatedly; instead use your Q Blinding Shot on his farming attempts to deny stacks and force him to miss CS, not to win a health trade. At levels 2 and 3 the lane is genuinely skill-based: you have poison poke compounding with Move Quick repositioning, but he now has Spirit Fire to shred your armor if you stand near a wave, and your health pool is too small to let his E hit you and then take a Q to the face.

notes: Two things I deliberately did NOT write. (1) The existing text in content.early and wants.you[0] assumes Blinding Dart stops Siphoning Strike from landing and denies the stack. Blind makes basic attacks miss, and Siphoning Strike is an empowered basic attack — but the wiki explicitly carves out "some empowered basic attacks" from the miss and does not document Nasus's case either way, so whether the stack and the cooldown are consumed is UNVERIFIED. I left those existing lines untouched rather than reinforce a claim I could not confirm; it is worth a dedicated check, because a large amount of Teemo-vs-Nasus advice on this site rests on it. (2) _missing-interactions.json raises a "resistances-invalidated" rule for Fury of the Sands. Its percent-max-health damage is aimed at the target's own health pool, and Teemo's is one of the smallest in the game, so that aura is not what kills him here — the Q is. I wrote the R up for its cooldown-halving and attack-range effects instead, which are the parts that actually change Teemo's spacing.
